blocks.prompt: 7. Prove that the lines represented by the equation \(9y^{2} + 6xy + x^{2} = 0\) are coincident.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh 'prove' wala sawal hai: humein saabit karna hai ke dono lines coincident hain.
Coincident ka matlab hai dono lines ek doosre ke bilkul upar, yani asal mein ek hi line.
Diya kya hai? Joint equation. Rule: Theorem 8, jis mein \(h^{2} = ab\) ho to lines coincident hoti hain.
Dhyan dein: terms ulti tarteeb mein likhe hain, pehle \(y^{2}\) phir \(x^{2}\).
Plan: tarteeb theek karna, \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhna, \(h^{2} - ab = 0\) dikhana, aur perfect square bana kar woh ek line bhi nikal lena.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(9y^{2} + 6xy + x^{2} = 0\).
Saabit karna: is ki lines coincident hain.
Tareeqa: Theorem 8 kehta hai \(h^{2} = ab\) ho to lines real aur coincident hoti hain. Yeh test seedha coefficients par chalta hai, is liye sab se tez hai.

Standard tarteeb mein likhein
\[x^{2} + 6xy + 9y^{2} = 0\]
\[a = 1,\quad 2h = 6 \Rightarrow h = 3,\quad b = 9\]
Kyun: \(a\) hamesha \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient hai aur \(b\) \(y^{2}\) ka, terms chahe kisi bhi tarteeb mein chhape hon.
Dhyan dein: pehla number 9 dekh kar \(a = 9\) likhna aam ghalti hai; yahan \(a = 1\) hai.

\(h^{2} - ab\) ka test
\[h^{2} - ab = 9 - (1)(9) = 0\]
Kyun: \(h^{2} = ab\) bilkul Theorem 8 ka coincident wala case hai. Saath hi angle formula mein numerator zero, to \(\tan\theta = 0\) aur angle \(0^{\circ}\).

Woh ek line nikalein
\[x^{2} + 6xy + 9y^{2} = (x + 3y)^{2} = 0\]
\[x + 3y = 0 \text{ (do dafa)}\]
Kyun: \(p^{2} + 2pq + q^{2} = (p + q)^{2}\), jahan \(p = x\) aur \(q = 3y\). Dono factors ek jaise hain, yani dono lines ek hi line \(x + 3y = 0\) hain.

Tasdeeq:
\[(x + 3y)^{2} = x^{2} + 6xy + 9y^{2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: square khola to di gayi equation wapas aa gayi. Do alag raaston (test aur perfect square) se ek hi natija, to saboot mukammal.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(h^{2} - ab = 0\), is liye lines coincident hain; dono \(x + 3y = 0\) hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Answer key mein number 7 hai hi nahi (list 6 ke baad seedha 8 par jati hai), is liye is sawal ka koi chhapa hua jawab nahi. Upar wala jawab hamara hai, aur \((x + 3y)^{2}\) khol kar check kiya gaya hai.
